rules.title: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B (limits on charges before tenancy)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord (lessor) may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock-change fee. Application, screening, pet, cleaning and amenity fees charged by landlords are barred.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit and locks may be charged
rules.penalty: Treble damages and attorney's fees (as awarded in Perry v. Equity Residential Management, a federal district court case)
rules.status_basis: Described as in effect since the 1970s

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords (lessors) of residential tenancies.

rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks ( MGL Ch 186 Section 15B ).

rules.title: 254 CMR 7 (broker regulations on fees to prospective tenants)
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge application or finding fees to prospective tenants. They must give the applicant written notice of the fee amount, the time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, at the first personal meeting.

requires.name: broker_bound_party
requires.text: The regulation binds licensed brokers or salespersons, not landlords

coverage.summary: Applies to licensed real estate brokers dealing with prospective tenants.

rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
